page: Microsoft Azure E192ds_v7 is an Edsv7-family virtual machine configured with 192 vCPUs and 1536.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processors running at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this server features 96 physical cores with hyper-threading. The hardware includes a substantial 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated vector and matrix operations.

For storage-intensive tasks, the instance is bundled with 11339 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier memory bandwidth, achieving top 10% performance in both small-block cached and large-block uncached read-only operations, alongside strong write performance. This high memory throughput is complemented by top-tier multi-threaded decompression and static web serving capabilities.

Multi-core compute benchmarks, including stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests, place the server in the top 10% tier, although single-core performance remains in the average range. Database and in-memory operations are highly efficient, with Redis SET operations and Passmark database benchmarks scoring in the top tier. Large language model inference benchmarks show strong prompt processing speeds, particularly for large 70B models, though text generation speeds are average to weak.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E192ds_v7 offers high resource density by combining massive memory capacity with extensive local NVMe storage on a single virtualized host. This configuration is highly suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching layers, enterprise resource planning systems, and heavy data-processing pipelines that require high memory-to-CPU ratios without requiring dedicated GPU acceleration.
